releases.name: v0.16.17 — Readable Grip decisions without line breaks
releases.body:
# v0.16.17 — Readable Grip decisions without line breaks

## Changes

- Make new native Grip questions readable even when OpenCode collapses newlines and blank lines. Icons, textual labels and visible ` ┃ ` separators distinguish the retained original-request excerpt, current decision and reason. English uses matching labels; meaning does not depend on emoji rendering or color.
- Instruct Mission controllers to keep the decision and reason concise while preserving material targets, actions, exclusions and cost/retention conditions. Detailed background can precede the Form in ordinary chat, without another question. The host does not truncate authorization conditions or infer semantic sections inside arbitrary prose.
- Preserve normal option labels/descriptions/order, the permanent consultation choice, saved native question identity, free-form steering and hold/resume behavior. Already saved/open offers retain their old text and accept matching legacy retries. Only new offers receive the new display format.

## Review and verification

PR #355 addresses the user's actual display report and follows a consultation in their existing ChatGPT conversation. Five new/updated layout assertions failed before correction. The related Grip/initialization/V2 selection passed 147 tests; its fixed development commit passed 2,624 tests with 4 skipped, and Linux/Windows CI succeeded. Existing code/security review channels contained no concrete findings. Those development results are retained for their actual commit, not relabelled as release-candidate results.

An actual bundled OpenCode V2 native Form rendered the synthetic decision with `white-space: normal`; icons, labels and separators survived. The actual native consultation answer reached the candidate handler and retained the hold. The screenshot was shared with ChatGPT and passed its final visual evaluation. Narrow-width density remains a native typography/wrapping limitation. This does not claim model instruction adherence, model E2E or full native QuestionTool-executor coverage.

## Release scope

Fix one integrated `main` commit and one archive/SHA-256 before candidate preflight, mandatory full validation, same-commit Linux/Windows CI and actual Worker/model startup. Use the identical archive for both global CLI prefixes, OpenCode's config-local package, GitHub Release and one npm publication. Preserve model overrides and unrelated settings. Shared OpenCode restart remains user-controlled; confirm loaded identity afterward.

Release receipts, costs, package identity and cleanup observations are retained under `_testenv/releases/0.16.17/`. No GUI/CSS changes, hidden-Unicode line-break workaround, new approval gate or automatic external connector are introduced. See [Grip scope and compatibility](../grip.md).

## Verified candidate

- Commit: `f730de26fe35a0fba55e056988d7194e3ac42d05`.
- Archive SHA-256: `86d3171291c9788390771be76a0d99ee13c8e9ae8160fe623ddce794fd4eb2bc`.
- Linux full: 2624 passed, 4 skipped, 137 files. Windows CI: 55/55 passed on the same commit.
- Actual Worker: `openai/gpt-6.1-terra#max`, startup 17177 ms; Operator `openai/gpt-6.1-sol#xhigh`. Startup usage estimate $0.05384240; 2 unpriced requests. Final-archive startup only.
- Existing PR bodies/reviews/ordinary/inline comments collected and classified; no outstanding findings. Shared service not automatically restarted.

releases.name: v0.16.16 — Grip decision holds and native consultation
releases.body:
# v0.16.16 — Grip decision holds and native consultation

## Changes

- Add Grip to an active V2 Mission's existing single-choice native question explicitly marked `header: "Grip"`, issued by its Operator or Coordinator. Retain a labelled excerpt of the original user request and a permanent outside-consultation choice. Ordinary questions, input collection, permissions and non-controller sessions are unchanged; unmarked direction questions can still be missed.
- Persist the exact native offer and held direction in the existing Mission state. Consultation pauses new direction-changing planning, implementation, Review and acceptance, plus controller writes and authoring shell. Reads, status, consultation, cancellation and existing Workers' execution, cleanup and settlement remain available.
- Resume only from a fresh corresponding revised Grip question's listed normal choice. Retain free-form steering without silently treating it, stale calls, dismissals, quoted output or external advice as execution permission. Save failures and unavailable native history retain the hold without disabling observation.
- Serialize both initial and revised form admission, reject reused native identities with changed forms, and bind answers/recovery to the same live Mission. No additional approval ritual, GUI, automatic external transmission, Worker kill or budget/permission bypass.

## Review and verification

PR #352's four existing findings were reproduced and corrected: changed-form identity reuse, observation during recovery outages, concurrent initial offers and concurrent revised offers. Related initialization/Grip/V2 selection passed 143 tests; the final development commit passed 2,620 tests with 4 skipped, and Linux/Windows CI succeeded. These are development results, not relabelled as fixed-release validation.

The real OpenCode V2 2.2.2 native Form rendered and accepted the augmented choices in a zero-inference probe. Its blank-line display normalization is accepted. Pinned-source and adapter checks cover inner Code Mode hooks; neither probe claims model E2E, full native QuestionTool-executor coverage, instruction adherence or performance improvement. See [Grip scope and verification boundaries](../grip.md).

## Release scope

Fix one integrated `main` commit and one archive/SHA-256 before candidate preflight, full validation and actual Worker/model startup. Apply that same archive to both global CLI prefixes and OpenCode's config-local package, publish it to GitHub Release and npm once, and preserve model overrides and unrelated settings. Shared OpenCode restart remains user-controlled; loaded-version verification follows that restart.

Release receipts, costs, archive identity and cleanup observations are retained under `_testenv/releases/0.16.16/`. A Worker-startup fixture does not establish real-development completion or official benchmark scoring.

releases.name: v0.16.15 — Complete validation proof and native quiescence recovery
releases.body:
# v0.16.15 — Complete validation proof and native quiescence recovery

## Changes

- Require all declared ordinary-Worker checks, not only the terminal criterion, before settlement, Review and acceptance. Retain command order, cwd, actual outcomes and live input bindings. Missing, failed or stale checks cannot become full proof; genuine successful retries remain possible.
- Synchronize native Reviewer recipe corrections with formal goal registration, including reload. Reusable cached PASS evidence retains original proof IDs in the registration path; its skip notice is not represented as another check execution. Current binding checks still apply.
- Reconcile stale V2 background-launch status only with a unique same-session shell/job ID, command and native completion notification. Match freshness from invocation start, so short jobs ending before launch completion can release quiescence. Missing terminal proof still blocks overlapping writers; foreground validation exits and durable native history are unchanged.
- Reconcile missed after hooks before direct replan/handoff and provide an actionable result for unavailable initial-author self-recheck, without treating it as independent approval.
- Correction admission inherits the current unit's input/write declaration rather than resurrecting superseded historical Review scopes. Old Review context and failed evidence remain preserved.

## Review and verification

PR #349's existing P1 finding (cached PASS rejected by registration validation) was reproduced and corrected with original-proof provenance and current-binding regression coverage. Related plugin/retry selection: 231 PASS. PR #350's P2 finding (valid terminal notification before launch end rejected) reproduced in five cases; the corrected V2 selection passed 99 tests. The previously uncommitted retired-scope correction was copied into an isolated worktree, reproduced before correction and verified without editing the original worktree.

Pre-existing development SourceReview findings and their author self-rechecks remain distinct from independent post-fix approval. All existing PR bodies, reviews and ordinary/inline comments are collected and classified. Final release evidence is a fresh full suite and same-commit Linux/Windows CI, not earlier development PASS counts.

## Release scope

One integrated main commit and one archive/SHA-256 are fixed before candidate preflight, full validation and actual Worker/model startup. That same archive is used for both global CLI prefixes, OpenCode's config-local package, GitHub Release and one npm publication. Preserve model overrides, unrelated settings, the original dirty worktrees and earlier hotfix/rollback evidence. Shared service restart remains user-controlled.

Worker startup and generic fixture results do not establish completion of the original external-project tasks or official benchmark scoring. Receipts, costs, package identity and remaining observations are retained under `_testenv/releases/0.16.15/` in the isolated release worktree, with an evidence alias in the original repository.

releases.name: v0.16.14 — Git identity commits and validation binding recovery
releases.body:
# v0.16.14 — Git identity commits and validation binding recovery

## Changes

- Recognize commits with invocation-local `-c user.name=<literal>` and `-c user.email=<literal>` settings. Keep native Location/workdir whole-index inspection, preceding explicit adds, caller prohibitions and parallel Git-mutation restrictions. Arbitrary Git configuration, repository/index overrides, unsupported commit forms and active substitutions remain refused.
- Preserve Git ambiguity for Bash input/output process substitutions, including internal separators. Quoted literal values and non-Git native investigative commands retain their existing behavior.
- Explain exit-zero validation failures when declared read inputs change during execution. Direct completion retains the specific recovery instruction: inspect real inputs/outputs, prepare genuine generated inputs, or repair an estimated output-only read scope in the same Mission. Historical failed checks and freshness requirements are not relaxed.
- Correct cwd-only validation registration when the initial frozen contract already contains an explicit cwd. Keep frozen JSON property order across external/original/omitted/restored cwd registrations without changing admission identity, budget, source scope or old evidence.

## Review and verification

- PR #346: root source inspection and existing completed GitHub code/security reviews found no outstanding findings. Its earlier development SourceReview found process-substitution paths; the final head includes their corrections and regressions. The correcting reviewer's self-recheck is not a separate independent post-fix approval.
- PR #347: root source inspection and existing completed GitHub code/security reviews found no findings. The author also records an independent source review without Major/Medium findings.
- Existing PR validation is retained as development evidence: #346 plugin selection 223 PASS; #347 related selection 203 PASS / 2 conditional Docker skips and quick suite 667 PASS. The integrated release commit receives a fresh mandatory full suite and same-commit Linux/Windows CI; counts from earlier candidates are not final-release counts.
- Final receipts, source/archive identities, review dispositions, actual Worker/model startup and usage estimates are retained under `_testenv/releases/0.16.14/`.

## Release scope

One integrated main commit and one `.tgz`/SHA-256 are fixed before candidate preflight, the mandatory full suite and native Worker/model startup. The same archive is installed into both global CLI prefixes and OpenCode's config-local dependency, attached to GitHub Release and published once to npm. Existing model overrides and unrelated settings are preserved.

Fixture success and Worker startup do not establish completion of the original external-project tasks or formal benchmark scoring. Shared OpenCode service restart remains user-controlled; installed identity and shared-host loaded identity are reported separately.

releases.name: v0.16.13 — Native Git index and mkdir operand fixes
releases.body:
# v0.16.13 — Native Git index and mkdir operand fixes

## Changes

- Inspect the repository actually selected by native shell Location/workdir before a Git commit, including authorized external clones and subdirectory execution. Inspect the whole index with `--no-relative`; preflight never stages, unstages or commits files.
- Include preceding explicit `git add` paths in the prospective index. Preserve scope and explicit caller prohibitions, including when the Mission project and native Location differ. Command-local directory/index overrides and unsupported Git mutation forms retain their existing refusal behavior.
- Reconcile Git's physical repository paths with symlinked workspace and external-clone spellings. Resolve workspace-root aliases while preserving index-relative pathname components; retain physical and authorized alias paths for caller checks.
- Authorize staged symbolic links as directory entries, including dangling links. Entry authorization does not grant writes through their targets. Existing ordinary file-write checks remain in force.
- Preserve missing directory scope components and compare indexed paths independently of current working-tree directory symlinks. Neither a missing directory nor a replaced ancestor can authorize unrelated staged entries.
- Parse `mkdir -m` / `--mode` values separately from directory operands, including attached values, combined flags and `--`. Fix the observed native command being rejected for a nonexistent `<workdir>/700` write, while retaining checks on every actual directory and redirect.

## Review and verification

PR #343 initially had two valid P2 findings: symlinked workspace paths were incorrectly rejected, and staged links were treated as target writes. Both were reproduced against `50d523fca15078c614da5a216926ec8c5998b32d`. Follow-up review found two valid regressions in the first correction (`87186f1`): missing directory scopes widened to their existing ancestor, and mutable working-tree ancestry could change indexed-path authorization. Both were also reproduced before correction. The final plugin, manifest, shell-workdir and shell-sink selection passed 242 tests in 21.662 seconds, reusing the successful unchanged build after correcting fixture-only index cleanup. A real Git add from a symlinked native cwd verifies prospective physical-cwd semantics. Existing wrong-clone, staged-out-of-scope, caller-prohibition, command-context and real fixture-commit coverage is retained.

The final integrated main commit and one `.tgz`/SHA-256 are fixed before candidate preflight, the mandatory full suite and actual Worker/model startup. The same archive is used for global installation, GitHub Release and one npm publication. Final receipts, review dispositions, failure/success logs and model cost records are retained under `_testenv/releases/0.16.13/`.

The additional `mkdir` failure was recovered from the saved native tool input and reproduced before correction. The plugin, shell-mkdir, shell-workdir, shell-sink and release-profile selection passed 230 tests in 30.409 seconds including build. The regression covers the original compound command, mode syntax variants, real numeric/dash-named operands, redirect scope checks and actual Linux creation with mode `0700`. This runtime correction supersedes the unpublished Git-only archive; the new archive receives fresh release gates.

The fixture's actual Git commit and symlink regressions are model-free checks, not replay of the original user's separate-clone task or formal benchmark scoring. The final-archive native CLI gate verifies startup/model identity. Existing model overrides and unrelated global settings are preserved; running shared-host identity is verified separately after a user-chosen restart.
